status.nb: 118 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Bandits in Zamfara have declared no-go areas and imposed a N50 million levy on communities ahead of the 2027 elections, while gunmen have repeatedly set secondary schools ablaze in Plateau, including a Bokkos school. In Gombe, Air Force personnel allegedly opened fire on civilians, causing deaths and injuries, and in Benue military forces rescued two abducted women. ISWAP suffered a major loss with a Shura Council member and top commanders killed as troops repelled an attack in Borno. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Banditter i Zamfara har erklært no-go-områder og innført en N50 millioners avgift på lokalsamfunnene før valget i 2027, mens væpnede menn gjentatte ganger har satt brann på videregående skoler i Plateau, inkludert en skole i Bokkos. I Gombe skal luftforsvarets personell ha åpnet ild mot sivile, noe som har ført til dødsfall og skader, og i Benue reddet militære styrker to bortførte kvinner. ISWAP led et stort tap da et medlem av Shura-rådet og toppkommandanter ble drept da tropper avverget et angrep i Borno. Konflikten registrerte 1 486 dødsofre i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
